sections.name: 1.1 Introduction: Role of Business in the Development of an Economy

concepts.text: Business as the economic activity of producing and exchanging goods and services to earn profit
How business drives economic development: production, employment, income and wealth creation

sections.name: 1.2 History of Trade and Commerce in India

concepts.text: Ancient India's trade links by land and sea; Silk Route and maritime trade with distant regions
Indigenous banking: hundi as a negotiable credit instrument and chitti; role of the money-lending sahukar
Kinds of hundi (e.g. dhani-jog, shah-jog, firman-jog) as a recall/application item
Rise of intermediaries: commission agents, brokers and distributors who financed and bore risk
Transport by land and water (roads, rivers, coastal shipping) enabling trade
Trading communities and merchant guilds/corporations (shreni) and their self-regulation
Major trade centres of ancient India (e.g. Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjain, Surat, Broach, Tamralipti, Kaveripatnam)
Major exports (spices, textiles, indigo, gems) and imports (horses, precious metals, wine) of ancient India

Post-1991 economic reforms and India's re-emergence as a fast-growing economy
Meaning of economic vs non-economic activities
Features of business: economic activity, production/procurement, sale/exchange, regularity of dealings, profit motive, uncertainty of returns, element of risk

sections.name: 1.4 Comparison of Business, Profession and Employment

concepts.text: Meaning of profession (specialised knowledge, professional body, code of conduct) and employment (working for wages/salary)
Comparison on mode of establishment, nature of work, qualification, reward, capital, risk, transfer of interest, code of conduct
Industry vs commerce as the two broad groups of business activity
Primary industries: extractive and genetic industries
Secondary industries: manufacturing (analytical, synthetical, processing, assembling) and construction
Tertiary/service industries supporting primary and secondary sectors
Commerce = trade + auxiliaries to trade; removal of hindrances of person, place, time, finance, risk and information
Trade: internal (wholesale, retail) and external (import, export, entrepot)
Auxiliaries to trade: transport, banking and finance, insurance, warehousing, communication, advertising
Role of profit: survival, growth, reward for risk, reputation

Multiple objectives in key areas: market standing, innovation, productivity, physical and financial resources, earning profits, manager performance and development, worker performance and attitude, social responsibility

Meaning of business risk as uncertainty causing loss
Nature: arises from uncertainties, essential part of every business, degree depends on nature and size, profit is reward for risk
Causes: natural, human, economic, other (political, mechanical) causes
Speculative vs pure risk distinction

sections.name: 1.8 Starting a Business: Basic Factors (book section)

concepts.text: Basic factors: selection of line of business, size of firm, choice of form of ownership, location, financing, physical facilities, plant layout, competent workforce, tax planning, launching the enterprise
Short-answer questions: distinguish business, profession and employment; define auxiliaries
Long-answer questions: explain characteristics of business, causes of business risk, need for multiple objectives
Classify given activities as industry, commerce, trade or auxiliary; identify type of industry from a case
Project/activity: trace trade history or prepare a chart of trade centres and goods traded
Meaning of form of business organisation and the main forms available in India
Meaning of sole proprietorship
Features: formation and closure, liability (unlimited), sole risk bearer and profit recipient, control, no separate entity, lack of business continuity
Merits: quick decision making, confidentiality, direct incentive, sense of accomplishment, ease of formation and closure
Limitations: limited resources, limited life, unlimited liability, limited managerial ability

sections.name: 2.3 Joint Hindu Family Business (Hindu Undivided Family)

concepts.text: Meaning: business owned by members of an HUF governed by Hindu Succession Act; coparceners and the karta
Dayabhaga (West Bengal) vs Mitakshara systems of inheritance
Features: formation, liability (karta unlimited, others limited), control by karta, continuity, minor members
Merits: effective control, continued business existence, limited liability of members, increased loyalty and cooperation
Limitations: limited resources, unlimited liability of karta, dominance of karta, limited managerial skills
Meaning and definition under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932
Features: formation by agreement, liability, risk bearing, decision making and control, continuity, number of members, mutual agency
Merits: ease of formation and closure, balanced decision making, more funds, sharing of risks, secrecy
Limitations: unlimited liability, limited resources, possibility of conflicts, lack of continuity, lack of public confidence
Types of partners: active, sleeping/dormant, secret, nominal, partner by estoppel; minor as partner (benefits only)
Types of partnership by duration: partnership at will vs particular partnership
Types by liability: general vs limited partnership; Limited Liability Partnership concept
Partnership deed: meaning and typical contents (name, capital, profit ratio, duties, interest, salaries, dissolution)
Registration of partnership: optional but consequences of non-registration; registration procedure with Registrar of Firms
Meaning and registration under the Cooperative Societies Act, 1912 (or state act)
Features: voluntary membership, legal status, limited liability, control (one member one vote), service motive
Merits: equality in voting, limited liability, stable existence, economy in operations, support from government, ease of formation
Limitations: limited resources, inefficiency in management, lack of secrecy, government control, differences of opinion
Types: consumer, producer, marketing, farmers', credit and cooperative housing societies
Meaning of a company under the Companies Act, 2013; artificial person with perpetual succession
Features: artificial person, separate legal entity, formation, perpetual succession, control by board, limited liability, common seal, risk bearing
Merits: limited liability, transfer of interest, perpetual existence, scope for expansion, professional management
Limitations: complexity in formation, lack of secrecy, impersonal work environment, numerous regulations, delay in decision making, oligarchic management, conflict in interests
Private company: features (member limits, restriction on transfer, no public invitation) and privileges
Public company: features and differences from a private company
One Person Company (OPC): meaning and key features
Comparison chart of all forms of organisation

sections.name: 2.7 Formation of a Company: Stages and Key Documents (per CBSE syllabus)

concepts.text: Stages in formation: promotion, incorporation (and for public companies, capital subscription/commencement as described in book)
Promoter: meaning and functions (identifying opportunity, feasibility studies, approving name, fixing signatories to MoA, appointing professionals, preparing documents)
Key documents: Memorandum of Association and its clauses (name, registered office, objects, liability, capital)
Articles of Association as internal rules; difference between MoA and AoA
Other incorporation documents: consent of proposed directors, statutory declaration, payment of fees; certificate of incorporation as conclusive evidence

sections.name: 2.8 Choice of Form of Business Organisation

concepts.text: Factors: cost and ease of setting up, liability, continuity, management ability, capital considerations, degree of control, nature of business

Mixed economy of India: coexistence of private and public sectors
Private sector: enterprises owned by individuals or groups (sole trader, partnership, company, cooperative)
Public sector: enterprises owned, managed and controlled by central/state government

concepts.text: Transaction risks: default on order taking/giving, delivery and payment

chapters.title: Social Responsibilities of Business and Business Ethics

concepts.text: Meaning of social responsibility: business obligation to act in ways desirable to society
Social responsibility vs legal responsibility

Arguments for: justification for existence and growth, long-term interest, avoid government regulation, maintenance of society, availability of resources, converting problems into opportunities, better environment, holding business responsible for social problems
Arguments against: violation of profit-maximisation objective and burden on consumers
Arguments against: lack of social skills and lack of broad public support
Reality of social responsibility: forces making business responsive (threat of public regulation, labour movement, consumer consciousness, social standards, business education, professionalisation)
Economic, legal, ethical and discretionary responsibility with examples

concepts.text: Responsibility towards shareholders/owners and investors

sections.name: 9.1 Meaning and Types of Internal Trade

concepts.text: Internal trade: buying and selling within a country, no customs duty; wholesale vs retail trade

Services of retailers to consumers: regular availability, new products information, convenience, wide selection, after-sales services, credit facilities
